solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cut took effect spanning very little time

indicators.note: one piece spanning another stretches across it, so it sits around the other

parts.note: brakes or a policy that 'bit' took hold and had an effect
a sec is a very short moment, as in 'just a sec'

explanation.surface: A measure that cut deep worked within moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a noun but is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide into two halves is a particular way to cut something.

clue.text: What hiker needs to drive away wolves?

parts.note: to back is to drive a vehicle backwards, away
wolves hunt in a pack

explanation.surface: A walker asks what is needed to see off threatening wolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack carried on the shoulders is essential kit on a hike.

clue.text: In due course leading Conservative gets in touch

indicators.note: the pieces get in, so go inside, the phrase for in due course

parts.note: soon means in due course
a team that is up is leading

explanation.surface: A front-running Tory will eventually make contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touch' looks like making contact but means a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a trace or hint, as in a touch of garlic.

clue.text: A stock of cards collected by agents in Spanish region

indicators.note: the agents collect, so hold, the other pieces

parts.note: the CIA is the US agency of intelligence agents
a talon is the pile of cards left after the deal

explanation.surface: Spies in Spain gather up a deck of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-eastern autonomous community of Spain, capital Barcelona.

clue.text: RSC plot works including high-class Pygmalion perhaps

indicators.note: the reworked letters include, so take in, the extra piece
the letters are worked over, as a mechanism works, into a new order

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage, so it stands for high-class

explanation.surface: A Royal Shakespeare Company storyline that stars an upper-crust Pygmalion.
explanation.walkthrough: The RSC is the Royal Shakespeare Company, which makes a theatrical reading of Pygmalion (Shaw's play) natural; here he is the mythical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pygmalion carved a statue he fell in love with, so he is an example of a sculpting artist.

clue.text: Detain narcotic criminal to give evidence against

indicators.note: a criminal arrangement is a crooked, twisted one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arresting a drug-dealing criminal so he can testify for the prosecution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give evidence against' sounds like testimony in court; in medicine it means a sign that a treatment is unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a symptom that argues against a treatment shows it is inadvisable.

clue.text: Fat Greek character wearing hat

indicators.note: the letter is wearing the hat, so sits under, inside it

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A plump Greek in a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats and oils are members of the chemical class of greasy biological molecules.

clue.text: Warplane damaged leading to fuss

indicators.note: the first piece leads to, so comes before, the second

parts.note: torn means damaged
ado is fuss, as in much ado

explanation.surface: A crippled fighter jet causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panavia Tornado is a combat jet flown by the RAF and other air forces.

clue.text: Rehearse, with regard to being delayed

parts.note: re means with regard to
late means delayed

explanation.surface: Practising for a show, worried about running behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rehearse' suggests practising for a performance, but here it means recount.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a story in the older sense is to recount or narrate it.

clue.text: Bishops in sports ground such as 15, 20, 25

parts.note: Lord's is the London cricket ground
the linked answer at 15 is a black American spiritual

explanation.surface: Clergy at a stadium alongside three other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lords Spiritual are the Church of England bishops who sit in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior bishops who sit by right in Britain's upper chamber of Parliament.

clue.text: Aristocrat with sad show on daytime TV

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
feeling down means feeling sad

explanation.surface: A gloomy nobleman appearing on an afternoon television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNTDOWN is a long-running British afternoon words-and-numbers quiz show on Channel 4.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running British afternoon quiz programme on Channel 4 involving letters and numbers games.

clue.text: Fairy left in danger

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian mythology

explanation.surface: A fairy abandoned in a perilous situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean exposure to harm or risk.

clue.text: Drunk digger was in front

parts.note: a pick is a tool for digging
someone who led was in front

explanation.surface: An intoxicated labourer who was out ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is slang for intoxicated, from being steeped as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Express again left large number behind

indicators.note: the second piece is placed behind the first, so it comes after it

parts.note: politically, Reds are on the left
a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: A message sent again that left many people behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a fast train or delivery, but it means put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something out in a new version is to set it in words a second time.

clue.text: Body of law put number in prison

indicators.note: the abbreviation for number is put in the word for prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A legal code that sends a certain number of people to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Canon law is the body of rules of a church, so the word names a code of law.

clue.text: Something heard at Twickenham wows lethargic townies terribly

indicators.note: the letters are treated terribly, knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A rugby crowd's singing delights some sluggish city dwellers awfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the London stadium of English rugby union, where England fans famously sing this old spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiritual is the anthem England rugby supporters sing at their national stadium.

clue.text: Old flame's covering, stirring male angst

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An ex-lover's cover-up stirs up a man's anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old flame' suggests a former lover; it is literally an old-fashioned gas flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh hood fitted over a gas jet that glowed to give light in older lamps.

clue.text: Using numerical data I caught out some politicians

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the data word

parts.note: statistics are numerical data
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Using figures, the speaker exposed certain politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught out' looks like a phrase for exposing someone, but 'caught' is C and 'out' signals removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocates of strong central state control form a political camp.

clue.text: Tree from river in Germany

parts.note: the Tamar is a river forming the Devon–Cornwall border in England
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A tree taken from a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree bearing pods of tangy pulp used in cooking.

clue.text: Unfavourable commercial jingles?

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
jingles are short pieces of verse

explanation.surface: Annoying advertising songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions are unfavourable ones, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 15
Baleful look from the vile yes-man

indicators.note: the letters come from within the run of words

explanation.surface: A malevolent glare from a nasty sycophant.
explanation.definitionFit: A malicious stare believed to cast a curse.

clue.text: Worker has good bit of grub

parts.note: a prole is a member of the working class

explanation.surface: A labourer enjoys a decent snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' suggests food, but it is the larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubby fleshy leg on a caterpillar's abdomen, part of a larva's body.

clue.text: Stuffed pasta recipe see soaked in garlic dressing

parts.note: R is the old abbreviation for recipe (Latin 'take') on prescriptions

indicators.note: one piece is soaked in, so surrounded by, the dressing

parts.note: aioli is a garlic mayonnaise
v. stands for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: A recipe telling the cook to see the pasta drenched in garlic mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pasta parcels filled with meat or cheese.

clue.text: Some stars working round carnival site

indicators.note: the word for working goes round the city

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
Rio de Janeiro hosts a famous carnival

explanation.surface: Celebrities performing at the carnival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests celebrities but means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hunter is a prominent constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: See 15
Disease, gruesome mostly, Goons originally introduced

indicators.note: one letter is introduced into the shortened word
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: lurid details are gruesome ones

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word Goons

explanation.surface: A grisly illness brought in by the Goons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goons' is apt: the word was coined on The Goon Show, a 1950s BBC radio comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A made-up word for an unspecified illness, popularised by a radio comedy.

clue.text: Releases hunter set loose

indicators.note: the letters are set loose and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A hunter frees animals he has trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfastening a rope or chain lets an animal go free.

clue.text: Pest letting off energy, having pinched female and left

indicators.note: the scrambled word has pinched, so holds, the two letters
letting off, like fireworks, explodes the word into a new order

explanation.surface: A pest-control story: something burns off energy after stealing a woman and fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting off energy' reads as a phrase for burning off steam, but 'letting off' is the anagram signal working on 'energy' to give GREENY.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid that infests garden plants is a common insect pest.

clue.text: When Parliament's not working on tax

parts.note: re means on, in the sense of concerning
a cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: Parliament's holidays come round when the subject is tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament's holiday break between sittings, when MPs are not in session.
